title: Security posture discovery with Tempest Fintech
summary: Initial security posture discovery for Tempest Fintech evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Covered SOC2/ISO status, SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC and audit logging, encryption (KMS/HSM), data residency/retention, and network/VPC options. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 report, security whitepaper, dedicated pricing, schedule SE deep-dive on private deployment and run a short benchmark POC.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
--- Meeting header ---
Date: 2026-03-17 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Tempest CTO), Sara Lin (Tempest Head of Security), Tom Redding (Platform), Priya Kaur (PM)

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Okay great, thanks everyone for joining, um, appreciate you taking the time. we've got Maya and Ethan from Redwood on the line. who do we have from Tempest?
[00:07] Raj: Hey this is Raj, CTO. Sara and Tom are here too. Priya is on for a couple minutes.
[00:12] Sara: Hi, thanks. we wanted to focus on your security posture specifically around SOC two, SAML, RBAC, KMS, and data retention, so sorry to be direct.
[00:20] Maya: No no that's perfect. that's exactly what we expected. quick agenda: we'll run through Redwood's certs and controls, talk SSO and provisioning, go into RBAC and audit logging, then Ethan can walk some network and private deploy details.
[00:32] Ethan: hey all. FYI I'm going to drop in a couple of architecture notes, um, especially around private / VPC options.
[00:38] Tom: good. quick context from us — we handle payments and PII, we run mostly in AWS in us-east-1, Okta for SSO, and we have a strict 90 day log retention policy by default but can extend for certain data.
[00:52] Maya: perfect. on certification front, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, um, we have a current report we can share under NDA, and we're pursuing ISO 27001 — audits are in progress, expected Q3.
[01:05] Sara: when you say SOC two Type two, is that covering hosted? and does it cover Dedicated/Private?
[01:12] Maya: good question — the SOC 2 Type II report covers Redwood's hosted control plane and our core hosted infra. for Dedicated we provide a managed offering where the dedicated pool is within our control plane and included; for Private/on-prem the customer controls infrastructure so some controls are customer-shared — we document shared responsibility in the security whitepaper.
[01:31] Raj: so for private we would need to bring our own HSM or KMS? we want key ownership.
[01:37] Ethan: yep, for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS or HSM — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs via standard PKCS or cloud KMS APIs. hosted can optionally do customer-managed keys for higher tiers — we have envelope encryption and KMS integration.
[01:55] Sara: envelope? sorry the transcription said envelope — can you clarify?
[01:58] Ethan: sure, we do envelope encryption: data keys are encrypted by a customer-managed KMS root key, so Redwood never has access to the raw root key.
[02:07] Priya: (quiet) ok makes sense
[02:10] [02:10] Maya: on SSO — we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. integrates with Okta, Azure AD, Ping, etc.
[02:20] Tom: great. does SCIM support group mappings to roles so we can mirror our internal RBAC?
[02:25] Ethan: yes, SCIM can provision groups and we map them to Redwood roles. our RBAC supports role hierarchy and custom roles. small caveat — some very granular permissions (e.g., token-level revoke) are currently limited to admin-type roles but we're expanding.
[02:42] Sara: about audit logs — what granularity and retention do you provide? we need per-request audit trail, who called what model, prompt content retention controls.
[02:52] Maya: we capture audit logs for admin actions, API keys, auth events, and request metadata. content retention is configurable per-customer: default short retention for hosted (30–90 days), long-term options for Dedicated/Private. we can redact prompts or enable no-retention modes for sensitive workloads.
[03:10] Raj: and are logs exportable to our SIEM? we use Splunk.
[03:14] Ethan: yes, logs stream to your SIEM via secure delivery — we support HTTPS delivery, S3 export, and direct SIEM connectors for common vendors.
[03:22] Sara: is the request content encrypted at rest?
[03:25] Maya: yes all data at rest is encrypted; for hosted it's AES-256 and keys are KMS-protected. in dedicated and private you can bring your own keys to control encryption at rest.
[03:36] Tom: network — do you allow VPC peering or private endpoints?
[03:40] Ethan: both. hosted supports private endpoints from VPCs, Dedicated supports dedicated GPU pools within a peered VPC, and Private is full customer VPC/on-prem. there are options for transit gateways, peering, and private link.
[03:52] Raj: okay timeline — we are aiming for a pilot in 6–8 weeks, production later this year, must be SOC2-compliant and Okta SSO in place.
[04:02] Maya: sounds reasonable. for the pilot we typically provide a short-lived dedicated environment or hosted with strict retention settings so you can run security reviews and benchmarks.
[04:12] Sara: about SOC two, we need to see the actual report and the last penetration test.
[04:16] Maya: absolutely — action: we'll share SOC 2 Type II report and recent pen test summary under NDA.
[04:21] [04:21] Priya: can you also share data residency docs?
[04:23] Maya: yes, we'll include region controls and data residency options.
[04:26] Ethan: quick technical note: when we talk about model KV cache, sometimes it's referred to as KV cache — we keep that in-memory and encrypted; by default it's ephemeral per session, and for some optimizations we persist short-term caches but those are encrypted and controlled by policies.
[04:41] Sara: persistence of cache is a concern if it stores PII
[04:44] Ethan: totally — we can disable caching for specific routes or the pilot.
[04:48] Raj: can we do customer-managed logging so none of the raw prompts go to Redwood-managed storage?
[04:54] Maya: yes, for dedicated/private we can route logs and raw prompts to your S3 or SIEM; hosted has options for no-retention or customer-managed keys depending on tier.
[05:05] Tom: compliance questions: do you have ISO 27001 cert?
[05:09] Maya: ISO 27001 is in progress, audit scheduled Q3; we can share scope and evidence where available.
[05:15] Sara: do you support RBAC integrations with our internal LDAP?
[05:19] Ethan: we support SAML/OIDC primarily for auth and SCIM for provisioning; for LDAP we recommend using an IdP bridge with SAML/OIDC, or we can work with your infra team on an integration pattern.
[05:32] Raj: any exports of raw token or embedding vectors? we're concerned about ML artifacts leaving our control.
[05:38] Maya: embeddings and artifacts are treated as data; we can configure retention and routing so vectors are stored in your environment for dedicated/private, and hosted can be configured to not persist embeddings or to store in customer-managed buckets.
[05:51] Priya: sandbox access — can we get a test account that mirrors our retention and SSO settings?
[05:55] Maya: yes, we'll spin up a sandbox with Okta SSO and the retention settings you want. usually a short-lived dedicated for pilot.
[06:03] Ethan: I'm going to share a quick screen of the architecture — (screen share start) — apologies if some diagrams are small.
[06:10] [06:10] Ethan: (explaining) here is hosted: control plane managed by Redwood, multi-tenant compute with tenancy isolation, default SOC 2 controls. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, network isolation, and optional customer-managed keys. Private: full VPC + on-prem where customer is responsible for hosting infra, and Redwood provides a private control plane or off-line installer.
[06:36] Raj: are there SLA differences?
[06:39] Maya: yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime; hosted has best-effort SLAs depending on plan; Private SLAs are part of the enterprise agreement.
[06:49] Sara: incident response — what's the play? do you provide runbooks and notify windows?
[06:54] Maya: we have an IR plan, notify customers based on severity (within 1 hour for sev-1), we provide postmortems and we can do joint IR exercises for enterprise customers.
[07:06] Tom: curious about tokenization and PII masking — any built-in redaction?
[07:11] Ethan: we offer pre-processing hooks you can run to strip or mask PII before it hits the model; customers often run a lambda or a preprocessor in their VPC for sensitive workloads.
[07:22] Raj: benchmarks — we want latency number for our typical 1k token requests, can you run a POC?
[07:27] Maya: yep, for pilot we can run a short benchmark using your prompt sets; Ethan will coordinate the test harness.
[07:33] Ethan: I'll need a sample prompt set and expected QPS/latency targets; I'll run on Dedicated and Hosted variants for comparison.
[07:40] Sara: legal & data residency: we may require data to stay in the US east region. is that doable?
[07:45] Maya: yes, we can pin to a region; Dedicated and Private make it easier to guarantee residency. hosted has region controls but may fall back in rare events; for strict residency Dedicated is preferred.
[07:58] Priya: timeline recap?
[08:00] Raj: pilot in 6–8 weeks and security review before pilot sign-off.
[08:05] Maya: action items and next steps will be: send SOC2 report + pen test, send security whitepaper + data residency docs, provide dedicated pricing and pilot setup, schedule SE deep-dive for private deployment and network design.
[08:18] Sara: ok that's good. couple more quick Qs — do you support token-level auditability? like which user triggered which token?
[08:26] Ethan: we log request metadata, API key/user mapping, and can surface token/user in audit logs. exact token contents are subject to retention policy and redaction options.
[08:36] Tom: do you support customer-controlled purging? we may need legal hold override.
[08:41] Maya: yes, we support purge APIs for customer data and retention overrides; for Private you fully control purging.
[08:49] Raj: pricing — can you ballpark dedicated monthly for our size?
[08:53] Maya: we'll send a tailored quote; rough ballpark depends on GPU class and baseline qps — we'll follow up in writing.
[08:59] Ethan: technical note — for private on-prem installs we do an install window and remote validation; we can support air-gapped installs with offline license keys.
[09:10] Sara: any customer references in finance you can share?
[09:14] Maya: yes we have a few anonymized references and case studies; we'll include those.
[09:19] Raj: ok if we sum up next steps: 1) Redwood share SOC2 + pen test, 2) Redwood share security whitepaper & region/residency docs, 3) Redwood provide dedicated pilot pricing + sandbox with Okta SSO, 4) schedule SE deep dive on private/VPC — is that right?
[09:34] Maya: yes exactly.
[09:36] Priya: can we try to get the SOC2 doc by Friday?
[09:39] Maya: yes we'll try; our AE will send the NDA and then the report.
[09:45] Sara: small nit — you said SCIM groups map to roles; can we get a sample mapping?
[09:50] Ethan: yep I'll attach a sample SCIM->RBAC mapping in the follow-up.
[09:56] Tom: last Q — are audit logs immutable?
[09:59] Maya: logs are append-only in our system; for Dedicated we can mirror to your immutable storage if required.
[10:07] Raj: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll review and get the questionnaire back to you.
[10:12] Maya: thanks — we'll follow up with docs and next steps.
[10:15] Ethan: thanks, bye.

--- End transcript ---

Note: transcript has occasional imperfect transcriptions (e.g., "SOC two" for SOC2, "K M S" for KMS, "K-V cash" for KV cache) and speaker interruptions typical of recorded sales calls.
